findings.documented: API key should be sent as ?api_key= query parameter
findings.actual: API requires X-API-Key request header. Using query parameter returns 400 with message: 'send your key in the X-API-Key request header, not as a query parameter'
findings.how_found: First API call using documented query parameter approach returned 400 error
findings.impact: Any client following the documentation will fail on every request

findings.documented: Login returns {token, token_type, expires_in: 86400, user: {email, name}} with token valid for 24 hours
findings.actual: Returns {access_token, refresh_token, token_type, expires_in: 900, refresh_url, user: {email}}. Token expires in 15 minutes (900s), not 24 hours. No 'name' field in user object. Has refresh_token and refresh_url fields not documented.
findings.how_found: Called POST /auth/login and compared response shape to documentation
findings.impact: Clients expecting 24-hour sessions will break after 15 minutes. Clients looking for user.name will get undefined.

findings.documented: Not mentioned anywhere in API_REFERENCE.md
findings.actual: POST /auth/refresh accepts {refresh_token} and returns a new access_token. The login response includes refresh_url: '/auth/refresh' pointing to this endpoint.
findings.how_found: Discovered refresh_url in login response, then called the endpoint
findings.impact: Without this endpoint, sessions die after 15 minutes with no way to renew without re-login

findings.documented: Invalidates the current token server side
findings.actual: Returns {ok: true, note: 'tokens are stateless; discard them client side'}. Tokens are NOT invalidated server-side; they are stateless JWTs.
findings.how_found: Called POST /auth/logout and read the response
findings.impact: Minor - logout is advisory only, tokens remain valid until expiry

findings.documented: Collection responses have shape {total, page, page_size, results} with page and limit query parameters. page is 1-indexed, limit max 200.
findings.actual: Response shape is {limit, offset, count, total, has_more, results}. Uses offset-based pagination, not page-based. The 'page' parameter is silently ignored (always returns offset=0). Limit is capped at 50 regardless of requested value.
findings.how_found: Requested page=2&limit=20, got offset=0 (same first page). Requested limit=200, got count=50.
findings.impact: Clients using page parameter will always see the first page. Clients requesting limit>50 will miss records.

findings.documented: Returns active sale listings. Inactive, expired and withdrawn listings are excluded server side.
findings.actual: Returns both active (is_live:true, 2627 records) and inactive (is_live:false, 673 records) listings. Total 3300 records, with is_live field present but undocumented.
findings.how_found: Fetched all listings via pagination and checked is_live field distribution
findings.impact: Frontend showing 'active' listings will actually display inactive properties unless filtering client-side

findings.documented: total is the exact number of records matching your filters
findings.actual: Reported total=3285 but fetching all pages yields 3300 records. Similarly for rentals (1239 vs 1250) and projects (375 vs 400). Fetched count is always higher than reported total.
findings.how_found: Paginated through all records using offset and compared final count to reported total
findings.impact: Clients relying on total for pagination math will stop fetching before reaching all records

findings.documented: furnishing parameter filters by unfurnished/semi-furnished/fully-furnished
findings.actual: The furnishing parameter is accepted (no 400 error) but silently ignored. GET /v1/listings?furnishing=semi-furnished returns total=3285, identical to unfiltered results.
findings.how_found: Compared total returned with furnishing filter vs without - both return 3285
findings.impact: Users filtering by furnishing see all listings, not just matching ones. Must filter client-side.

findings.documented: project_id can be used to filter listings for a specific project (implied by 'GET /v1/listings?project_id=...')
findings.actual: project_id parameter is silently ignored. GET /v1/listings?project_id=P60001 returns total=3285 (same as unfiltered).
findings.how_found: Tested project_id filter and compared total to unfiltered request
findings.impact: Cannot get listings for a specific project via API filter. Must filter client-side from full dataset.

findings.documented: Every listing_id is globally unique, and each listing corresponds to exactly one physical property
findings.actual: listing_ids are indeed unique, but multiple listing_ids correspond to the same physical property. 72 groups of duplicates found across different source websites (same lat/lng + bedroom + apartment_name, different listing_id and website).
findings.how_found: Clustered all 3300 listings by (latitude rounded to 4dp, longitude rounded to 4dp, bedroom, apartment_name) and found 72 groups with 2+ listings
findings.impact: Property count is inflated. 3300 listing records represent only 3228 unique physical properties.

findings.documented: Each listing describes a real property
findings.actual: 22 listings have physically impossible attributes: 6 with negative prices, 6 with carpet_area > super_built_up_area (physically impossible), 6 with floor > total_floors, and 4 with swapped lat/lng coordinates (latitude in longitude range and vice versa for Gurgaon).
findings.how_found: Systematic validation of all 3300 records checking: price<0, carpet_area>super_built_up_area, floor>total_floors, coordinates outside Gurgaon bounds with lat/lng swap detection
findings.impact: These records produce nonsensical data on property detail pages and corrupt aggregate statistics

findings.documented: Listings are genuine property listings
findings.actual: 457 listings are suspected lead-generation fakes. 34 phone numbers each appear on 10+ listings across 5+ different apartment complexes and 5+ different localities. The top offender has 33 listings across 33 different apartments in 10 localities. This pattern is characteristic of lead-gen operations that post fake listings to collect buyer enquiries.
findings.how_found: Grouped all listings by posted_by_contact, identified phones with 10+ listings where unique apartment count >= 5 and unique locality count >= 5
findings.impact: ~14% of all listings are potentially fake, inflating supply and misleading buyers

findings.documented: total_listings is recomputed whenever a listing is added or withdrawn, so it always agrees with what GET /v1/listings?project_id=... returns
findings.actual: 303 out of 400 projects have total_listings that disagrees with the actual count of listings referencing that project_id. Additionally, the project_id filter on /v1/listings is silently ignored, so the documented cross-check method doesn't even work.
findings.how_found: For each of the 400 projects, counted listings in the full dump with matching project_id and compared to the project's total_listings field
findings.impact: Project pages show incorrect listing counts, and there is no working API filter to verify them

findings.documented: Money is Indian rupees, integer, everywhere in the API. price_min and price_max are in rupees.
findings.actual: Project price_min and price_max are decimal numbers in crores (1 crore = 10,000,000 rupees), not integer rupees. Example: P60001 has price_min=1.66, price_max=4.54 meaning ₹1.66 Cr to ₹4.54 Cr.
findings.how_found: Inspected project records and found price values like 1.66, 4.54, 98.9 - clearly crores, not rupees
findings.impact: Frontend displaying project prices as rupees would show '₹2' instead of '₹2 Cr' - off by 7 orders of magnitude

findings.documented: GET /v1/listing/{listing_id} returns a single listing
findings.actual: Returns 404. The correct path is /v1/listings/{listing_id} (plural 'listings').
findings.how_found: Called GET /v1/listing/{id} and got 404; then tried /v1/listings/{id} which returned 200
findings.impact: Clients using the documented singular path will always get 404

findings.documented: Up to ten comparable listings — same locality, same bedroom count, price within 15%
findings.actual: Returns 404. This endpoint does not exist.
findings.how_found: Called GET /v1/listings/{listing_id}/similar and got 404
findings.impact: Cannot implement 'similar listings' feature as documented

findings.documented: GET/POST/DELETE /v1/favourites for saving listings per user
findings.actual: All three verbs return 404 on /v1/favourites. The working endpoint is /v1/saved (undocumented).
findings.how_found: Called GET /v1/favourites and got 404. Probed alternative paths and found /v1/saved returns 200.
findings.impact: Saved listings feature cannot be built using documented endpoints

findings.documented: Not mentioned in API_REFERENCE.md
findings.actual: GET /v1/saved returns {count, results: [listing objects]}. POST /v1/saved with {listing_id} saves a listing (returns 201). DELETE /v1/saved/{listing_id} removes it. This is the actual saved listings endpoint.
findings.how_found: Probed common alternative names after /v1/favourites returned 404
findings.impact: Saved listings feature works but only if you discover this undocumented endpoint

findings.documented: Pre-computed aggregates for your city including total_listings, median_price, by_locality, by_bhk
findings.actual: Returns 404. This endpoint does not exist. Also checked /v1/analytics, /analytics/summary, /v1/stats, /v1/summary, /v1/dashboard, /v1/insights - all 404.
findings.how_found: Called GET /v1/analytics/summary and got 404. Tried multiple alternative paths.
findings.impact: Insights/dashboard screen cannot use pre-computed analytics; must compute from full dataset

findings.documented: All timestamps are ISO 8601, UTC, Z suffix, everywhere in the API
findings.actual: The /health endpoint returns server_time with +05:30 offset (IST/Asia Kolkata), not UTC with Z suffix. Example: 2026-09-14T18:32:12.615735+05:30. However, listing posted_at timestamps do use Z suffix (UTC).
findings.how_found: Called GET /health and examined the server_time field timezone
findings.impact: Inconsistent timezone handling between endpoints; time-based calculations need careful conversion

findings.documented: Rental field is super_builtup_area (same as listings)
findings.actual: Listings use 'super_built_up_area' (with underscores between built and up) while rentals use 'super_builtup_area' (no underscore). Inconsistent field naming across endpoints.
findings.how_found: Compared field names from listing and rental response objects
findings.impact: Code that handles both listings and rentals needs to account for different field names for the same concept
